accepted.s: During the discharge of an electrochemical cell, which one of the following correctly describes the functions of the electrodes?
o: Anode undergoes reduction and cathode undergoes oxidation
Anode undergoes oxidation and cathode undergoes reduction
Both anode and cathode undergo oxidation
Both anode and cathode undergo reduction
accepted.x: During discharge, oxidation involving loss of electrons occurs at the anode, while reduction involving gain of electrons occurs at the cathode.
accepted.tq: Use the standard oxidation-at-anode and reduction-at-cathode rule.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding an electrolyte in a battery:
1. It permits the movement of ions between the electrodes.
2. It prevents direct contact between the electrodes.
3. It necessarily conducts electrons between the electrodes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: An electrolyte allows ions to flow and keeps the electrodes apart. It does not provide a direct electronic path between the electrodes.
accepted.tq: Separate ionic conduction through the electrolyte from electronic conduction through the external circuit.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lead-acid battery — Lead and lead peroxide electrodes with sulphuric acid electrolyte
Zinc-carbon cell — Rechargeable cell with lithium metal-oxide cathode
Ni-Cd battery — Sodium and cadmium electrodes
Flow battery — Solid electrolyte enclosed between two metal plates
accepted.x: Lead-acid batteries use lead and lead peroxide (PbO2) electrodes with sulphuric acid as the electrolyte.
accepted.tq: Match each chemistry with its characteristic electrodes and electrolyte.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s:
With reference to nickel-cadmium batteries, consider the following statements:
1. They are rechargeable.
2. They contain nickel and cadmium electrodes.
3. Their use has declined partly because cadmium is toxic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Nickel-cadmium batteries are rechargeable, use nickel and cadmium electrodes, and have become less common because of cadmium toxicity.
accepted.tq: Select all the technically consistent statements rather than relying on the familiar use of the battery.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Which one of the following batteries is correctly associated with a non-rechargeable cell commonly used in torches and clocks?
accepted.x: The zinc-carbon dry cell uses zinc and carbon and is generally non-rechargeable; it is commonly used in torches and clocks.
accepted.tq: Identify the chemistry from the combination of construction, rechargeability and common use.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Nickel-metal hydride batteries are distinguished from nickel-cadmium batteries mainly because they
o: replace cadmium with a metal hydride
use sulphuric acid instead of an alkaline electrolyte
use a liquid electrolyte stored in separate tanks
accepted.x: A nickel-metal hydride battery replaces cadmium with a metal hydride and is used in hybrid vehicles and portable electronics.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely named Ni-Cd and NiMH chemistries by their second electrode material.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic feature of lithium-ion NMC batteries?
o: A zinc-carbon electrode pair and non-rechargeability
A nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode and high energy density
A sulphuric acid electrolyte and lead peroxide cathode
A liquid electrolyte in external tanks with separately scaled power
accepted.x: Li-ion NMC batteries use a nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode and offer high energy density. They are used in electric vehicles and portable electronics.
accepted.tq: Use the cathode composition to distinguish NMC from other lithium and non-lithium chemistries.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Li-ion LFP batteries are particularly valued for which combination of characteristics?
o: Separate scaling of energy and power through tanks
High toxicity and short cycle life
accepted.x: Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4 or LFP) batteries are known for safety and long cycle life and are used in electric vehicles and renewable-energy storage.
accepted.tq: Match the chemistry with its defining performance advantage rather than with a generic battery use.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about sodium-ion batteries:
1. They avoid the use of cobalt, nickel and copper.
2. Their volumetric energy density is still below that of LFP batteries.
3. Existing lithium-ion factories can be adapted for their manufacture.
4. Their global manufacturing capacity was about 70 GWh in 2025 and is projected at about 400 GWh in 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sodium-ion batteries avoid cobalt, nickel and copper, have lower volumetric density than LFP, can use adapted Li-ion factories, and their capacity is stated as about 70 GWh in 2025 with a projection of about 400 GWh in 2030.
accepted.tq: Check both qualitative features and the quantitative capacity figures before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding sodium-ion batteries is NOT correct?
o: They can be used for low-cost energy storage.
They avoid cobalt, nickel and copper in the stated chemistry.
They are being considered for low-cost electric vehicles.
Their volumetric energy density is higher than that of LFP batteries.
accepted.x: The volumetric energy density of sodium-ion batteries is still below that of LFP batteries. The other statements describe their stated advantages or applications.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the negative question.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: A battery technology uses a solid electrolyte instead of a conventional liquid or gel electrolyte. Which of the following is the most appropriate description of this technology?
o: Zinc-carbon battery, which is necessarily rechargeable
Flow battery, in which energy and power are always inseparable
Solid-state battery, offering improved safety and higher energy density
Lead-acid battery, which contains no electrolyte
accepted.x: Solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte and are expected to provide better safety and higher energy density. They remain an emerging technology, including for electric vehicles.
accepted.tq: Infer the battery category from the electrolyte form and its associated performance benefits.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s: Why are flow batteries considered suitable for large grid-scale storage?
o: Their energy and power capacities can be scaled separately
They depend exclusively on solid electrodes without tanks
They are always lighter than lithium-ion batteries
They use no electrolyte at all
accepted.x: Flow batteries store liquid electrolytes in tanks and allow energy capacity and power capacity to be scaled separately. Vanadium redox is an example.
accepted.tq: Link the design feature—separate tanks—to the grid-storage advantage of independent scaling.
accepted.sec: Battery chemistries - lead-acid, Ni-Cd, Li-ion (NMC, LFP), sodium-ion, solid-state, flow

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Battery chemistry)
a. Lead-acid
b. Li-ion NMC
c. Li-ion LFP
d. Flow battery

List-II (Characteristic or application)
i. Safe chemistry with long cycle life
 ii. Grid-scale storage with separately scalable energy and power
 iii. Automotive starting and UPS
 iv. High energy density with nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode
accepted.x: Lead-acid is used for automotive starting and UPS; NMC has a nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode and high energy density; LFP is safe with long cycle life; flow batteries suit grid-scale storage.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the electrode arrangement in a conventional lithium-ion battery?
o: Lead anode and lead peroxide cathode
Zinc anode and carbon cathode only
Graphite anode and lithium metal-oxide cathode
accepted.x: The conventional lithium-ion battery uses graphite as the anode and a lithium metal-oxide material as the cathode.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general lithium-ion electrode pair from those of lead-acid, Ni-Cd and zinc-carbon cells.

accepted.s: In electric-vehicle batteries, which one of the following materials generally forms the anode, while lithium, nickel and cobalt are generally associated with the cathode?
accepted.x: Graphite generally forms the anode of EV lithium-ion batteries, while lithium, nickel and cobalt are among the commonly used cathode materials.
accepted.tq: Separate the anode material from the cathode elements in an EV battery.
accepted.sec: Battery raw materials - critical elements, lithium finds, KABIL, NCMM

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding lithium-ion battery cathodes:
1. Lithium, nickel and cobalt are usually used in the cathode.
2. Graphite is generally the anode material.
3. All four materials—lithium, nickel, cobalt and graphite—usually form the cathode.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Lithium, nickel and cobalt are generally cathode-associated materials, while graphite forms the anode. Graphite is therefore not part of the stated group of four cathode materials.
accepted.tq: Watch for the ‘all four’ trap when one listed material belongs to the anode.
accepted.sec: Battery raw materials - critical elements, lithium finds, KABIL, NCMM

accepted.s: Lithium carbonate (Li2CO3) is important in the battery sector because it is
o: the solid electrolyte used in all flow batteries
a key raw material for lithium-ion cells
the principal electrode material in nickel-cadmium batteries
accepted.x: Lithium carbonate is a white crystalline salt obtained from lithium minerals and brines and serves as a key raw material for lithium-ion cells. A fall in its price can reduce battery energy-storage costs.
accepted.tq: Identify the industrial role of the named chemical rather than its physical appearance.
accepted.sec: Battery raw materials - critical elements, lithium finds, KABIL, NCMM

accepted.s: A reduction in the price of lithium carbonate is most directly expected to reduce the cost of
o: sulphuric acid production for lead-acid cells only
accepted.x: Lithium carbonate is a key raw material for lithium-ion cells; falling prices can reduce the cost of battery energy-storage systems (BESS).
accepted.tq: Trace the input-cost relationship from the raw material to the battery-storage system.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Budget 2026–27 measures on critical minerals is correct?
o: Rare Earth Corridors are proposed exclusively in Karnataka and Gujarat.
Customs duty is imposed on all capital goods for critical-mineral processing, and Rare Earth Corridors are confined to Jammu and Kashmir.
Customs duty is exempted on capital goods for critical-mineral processing, and Rare Earth Corridors are proposed in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
The measures concern only lithium imports and do not include processing infrastructure.
accepted.x: Budget 2026–27 provides customs-duty exemption on capital goods for critical-mineral processing and proposes Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Check both parts of the policy statement—customs treatment and the complete list of corridor states.

B. Amaravati
C. Marlagalla, Mandya
D. Argentina acquisition by KABIL

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the concern regarding global critical-mineral supply chains?
o: More than 70% of lithium processing and most cobalt refining are concentrated in a few countries.
Only graphite processing is concentrated, while lithium and cobalt are geographically dispersed.
Lithium processing and cobalt refining are evenly distributed across all countries.
No significant concentration exists in the processing or refining of battery minerals.
accepted.x: More than 70% of lithium processing and most cobalt refining are concentrated in a few countries, creating a supply-chain risk for battery manufacturing.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute reversals of the stated concentration and identify the precise supply-chain risk.
